title: Intent-aware OpenAI ChatCompletions conformance & streaming-aware mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Implement an intent-aware request/response mapper that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) payloads and produces normalized Redwood internal chat request objects with explicit signaling for streaming frames, function/tool invocation intents, and structured output envelopes. Goals: preserve semantics for legacy clients, enable graceful degradation for tool-calls when backend models do not support function calling, and emit clear telemetry for mismatches. Approach: build a lightweight sidecar component (stateless) that performs: 1) request normalization (roles, name/metadata preservation), 2) intent detection heuristics for tool calls (explicit 'function' fields vs. inferred instruction), 3) streaming frame orchestration to map SSE/chunked OpenAI streams into Redwood event frames including partial function call arguments, and 4) response conformance checking to ensure structured outputs adhere to Redwood schema contracts. Deliverables: implementation + unit/integration tests, conformance test suite, an interoperability compatibility matrix, and a migration guide for customers using legacy chat-completions clients. Links: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/OpenAI+CC+Intentful+Mapper; design notes: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IntentMapperDraft; prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-proxy/pull/1487. Rationale: many enterprise customers still rely on OpenAI ChatCompletions clients and expect streaming/tool-calling behaviors; rather than forcing them to migrate immediately, this mapper reduces integration friction while protecting our internal structured-output guarantees.
comments: 2025-02-21 - spike complete: validated request shapes for 12 representative legacy clients (python-openai, node-openai, rotor-proxy). Found two common mismatches: (a) clients omit name on system messages, (b) function call arguments sometimes arrive split across stream chunks.
2025-02-24 - design review (PM+Design): agreed to include explicit 'intent_score' on mapped requests to aid routing to models that support functions. PM requested backward-compatible default of 0.0.

2025-02-27 - engineering notes: decided on greedy streaming reassembly buffer with 32KB per-stream soft cap to avoid unbounded memory. Trade-off: increases latency for ultra-low-latency tiny responses but reduces broken function-arg edge cases.
2025-03-01 - security review: no customer-secret extraction; verified we do not persist payloads. SSO audit checklist item assigned to infra (ENG-207336).

2025-03-03 - implementation: initial sidecar binary built, integration tests added to CI. Observability hooks emit mismatch-rate, partial-arg-repair-count, and conformance-failures counters. Need review on event-schema naming (cc_to_rw_stream_frame).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Mapper accepts v1 ChatCompletions request and produces Redwood chat request JSON with preserved role/name metadata. 2) Streaming: OpenAI SSE/ndjson stream maps to a sequence of Redwood event frames with deterministic assembly of function call args. 3) Tool/function calling: explicit function call requests are signaled with intent_score >= 0.5 and include reconstructed arguments; when backend model lacks function support, mapper marks fallback=true and attaches sanitized prompt. 4) Conformance checks run in CI and show <0.1% synthetic failure on representative sample corpus. 5) Migration docs published and integration test matrix added to compatibility playbook.
notes: Planned short-term mitigations for high-throughput customers: allow bypass mode (transparent passthrough) controlled via header X-RW-Compat: passthrough while customers migrate. Follow-ups: add opt-in strict-mode that rejects non-conformant client requests with 4xx and developer-friendly error payloads. Investigate hooking into Optimize's cache hints for conversation prefixes to reduce cost. Metrics to track: conversion-rate (legacy->native), downstream model errors attributed to malformed function args, and per-customer fallback rate. QA checklist includes fuzz-testing of chunk boundaries and tool-call nesting.
